plants.name: Euphorbia pulcherrima
plants.description: In the wild, poinsettia is a tall, open shrub or small tree. It reaches 3–4 metres in the seasonally dry forests of Mexico and Central America. In December it is topped with flaming red bracts that look like petals. The true flowers are tiny yellow-green clusters at their centre.
plants.bloomingSeason: Winter, with peak display in December
plants.location: Mexico and Central America (native range); widely grown as a Christmas plant worldwide
plants.funFact: The bright red parts of a poinsettia are not petals. They are modified leaves called bracts, which change colour as the plant gets ready to flower.

plants.name: Camellia sasanqua
plants.description: This glossy-leaved evergreen from Japan opens single, silky blooms in red, pink and white as the winter chill sets in. The petals drop one at a time and scatter across the ground like confetti.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late autumn to early winter (late October through December)
plants.location: Japan, in gardens and hedgerows; also widely cultivated in temperate regions
plants.funFact: In Japan the sazanka is a classic sign of winter. Its petals fall individually, unlike the whole-flower drop of the related Camellia japonica.

plants.name: Ceratopetalum gummiferum
plants.description: This Australian native shrub is covered in small creamy flowers in early summer. As each flower fades, its sepals swell into papery, ruby-red structures that glow against the dark green foliage. It is a natural fit for the southern-hemisphere festive season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer, with flowers opening from December
plants.location: Coastal and sandstone country of New South Wales, Australia
plants.funFact: The red "petals" are actually enlarged calyx lobes. They turn red after the small white flowers have finished.
